components.name: Alert
components.description: Displays a short, dismissible status message to draw attention to important information (success confirmations, warnings, errors, etc.). Reach for it when you need to surface feedback about the result of an action or the current state of the page.
components.notes: Danger-variant alerts use `role="alert"` for assertive screen-reader announcements; all other variants use `role="status"` for polite announcements.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual style and ARIA role of the alert. Defaults to `'neutral'`.

props.name: title
props.description: Optional heading rendered above the alert's description.

props.name: children
props.description: The alert's main message content.

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: Called when the user clicks the dismiss (×) button. If omitted, no dismiss button is rendered.

components.example:
<Alert variant="success" title="Changes saved">
  Your profile has been updated.
</Alert>

components.name: Avatar
components.description: Displays a person's picture, or their initials as a fallback when no image is provided or the image fails to load. Reach for it when representing a user or account in lists, headers, or comments.
components.notes: By default the avatar exposes the person's name to assistive tech (`role="img"` with `aria-label`, or image `alt` text); set `decorative` when nearby visible text already names the person, to avoid the name being announced twice.

props.name: name
props.description: The person's name. Always required — it's both the source for the fallback initials and the accessible/image alt text (unless `decorative` is set).

props.name: src
props.description: URL of the image to display. Falls back to initials if omitted or if the image fails to load.

props.name: size
props.description: Size of the avatar. Defaults to `'base'`.

props.name: decorative
props.description: Set when adjacent visible text already names the person, so the avatar shouldn't also be announced — avoids screen readers reading the name twice. When `true`, the avatar is hidden from assistive tech (`aria-hidden`, empty image `alt`, no `role`/`aria-label` on the initials fallback).

components.name: Badge
components.description: Renders a small, inline label used to tag an item with a status, category, or count (e.g. "New", "Beta", an unread count). Reach for it when you need a compact, non-interactive visual marker alongside other content.

props.name: children
props.description: The label content rendered inside the badge, typically a short word or count.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual style of the badge. Defaults to `'neutral'`.

components.name: Button
components.description: A clickable button styled to match the design system, for triggering actions such as submitting a form or opening a dialog.
components.notes: All standard button HTML attributes (`onClick`, `disabled`, `type`, etc.) are supported and passed through to the underlying `<button>` element.

props.name: children
props.description: Content rendered inside the button.

components.name: Card
components.description: A container that groups related content in a bordered, padded surface. Reach for it when laying out discrete blocks of content (list items, summary panels, dashboard tiles, etc.) that should read as a single unit. All standard `<div>` HTML attributes are supported and passed through to the underlying element.

props.name: children
props.description: Content rendered inside the card.

components.name: DateRangePicker
components.description: A paired start/end date selector, rendered as a `<fieldset>` containing two Input fields of type `date`. Reach for this whenever a user needs to pick a bounded date range (e.g. filtering a report by date). The component is controlled: it always reflects `value` and reports changes via `onChange`.
components.notes: Each field's bounds constrain the other to keep the range valid — the start field's `max` is the selected end date (or the `max` prop), and the end field's `min` is the selected start date (or the `min` prop). The two fields render as an `<fieldset>`/`<legend>` group so screen readers announce them as related, each field keeps its own label/`aria-invalid`/`aria-describedby` wiring via Input, and when `error` is set the fieldset itself gets `aria-describedby` pointing at a `role="alert"` error message. Date entry/keyboard interaction is provided by the browser's native `<input type="date">`.

props.name: label
props.description: Label grouping the two date fields, rendered as the `<fieldset>` legend.

props.name: value
props.description: The current start/end selection. This component is controlled — always pass `value` together with `onChange`.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called whenever either the start or end date field changes, with the full updated `{ start, end }` value (the other field's value is preserved).

props.name: startLabel
props.description: Label for the start date field. Defaults to `'Start date'`.

props.name: endLabel
props.description: Label for the end date field. Defaults to `'End date'`.

props.name: error
props.description: Validation error message. When set, renders a `role="alert"` message below the fields and marks the fieldset `aria-describedby` pointing at it.

props.name: min
props.description: Earliest selectable date (ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`) for the start field. The end field's effective minimum is the selected start date, falling back to this value.

props.name: max
props.description: Latest selectable date (ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`) for the end field. The start field's effective maximum is the selected end date, falling back to this value.

components.example:
<DateRangePicker
  label="Reporting period"
  value={range}
  onChange={setRange}
  min="2024-01-01"
  max="2026-12-31"
/>

components.name: Icon
components.description: Renders a single icon from the design system's icon registry as an inline SVG. Reach for it anywhere a small, currentColor-tinted vector graphic is needed (buttons, status indicators, etc.).
components.notes: By default the icon is purely decorative (`aria-hidden="true"`) since it has no accessible name. Pass `title` to expose it to assistive technology as a named image (`role="img"` with an SVG `<title>`) — do this when the icon conveys meaning that isn't otherwise available as text nearby (e.g. an icon-only button).

props.name: name
props.description: Which icon from the registry (see IconName) to render.

props.name: size
props.description: Rendered size of the icon. Defaults to `'base'`.

props.name: title
props.description: When provided, the icon becomes an accessible image with this as its accessible name (rendered as an SVG `<title>`, with `role="img"`). Omitted (the default) means the icon is treated as decorative and hidden from assistive tech via `aria-hidden`.

components.name: Input
components.description: A single-line text field with a required, associated label and optional inline validation error. Reach for this any time you need a labelled native `<input>` (text, email, date, etc. — via the native `type` prop) inside a form.
components.notes: The label is linked to the input with `htmlFor`/`id` (an id is auto-generated via `useId` if none is passed), and when `error` is set the input gets `aria-invalid="true"` plus `aria-describedby` pointing at the error message, which is itself rendered with `role="alert"`.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label rendered above the input and associated via `htmlFor`/`id`. Required (not optional) — this is the a11y rule the CI agent enforces: no unlabeled inputs are allowed.

props.name: error
props.description: Validation error message. When set, renders a `role="alert"` message below the input and marks the input `aria-invalid` with `aria-describedby` pointing at it.

components.example:
<Input
  label="Email address"
  type="email"
  value={email}
  onChange={(e) => setEmail(e.target.value)}
  error={emailError}
/>

components.name: Modal
components.description: A focused, modal dialog rendered into `document.body` via a portal, used to interrupt the user with a task or piece of information that requires their attention before continuing.
components.notes: The dialog exposes `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`, and `aria-labelledby` pointing at the title. While open, focus moves to the dialog, the Escape key calls `onClose`, and background scrolling is locked by setting `document.body.style.overflow`. On close/unmount, focus is restored to whatever element was focused before the modal opened. Note that focus is moved to the dialog container only — focus is not trapped/cycled within the dialog's interactive children.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the modal is currently visible. When `false`, the component renders nothing.

props.name: onClose
props.description: Called when the user requests to close the modal (Escape key, backdrop click, or the close button).

props.name: title
props.description: Heading content rendered in the modal header and linked to the dialog via `aria-labelledby`.

props.name: children
props.description: Body content rendered inside the dialog.

components.example:
<Modal open={isOpen} onClose={() => setIsOpen(false)} title="Delete item">
  Are you sure you want to delete this item?
</Modal>

components.name: Select
components.description: A native `<select>` dropdown with a required, associated label, an optional placeholder option, and optional inline validation error. Reach for this when a user must pick one value from a known, bounded list of options.
components.notes: The label is linked to the select with `htmlFor`/`id` (an id is auto-generated via `useId` if none is passed), and when `error` is set the select gets `aria-invalid="true"` plus `aria-describedby` pointing at the error message, which is itself rendered with `role="alert"`. Keyboard interaction (opening, arrow-key navigation, typeahead) is provided by the browser's native `<select>`.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label rendered above the select and associated via `htmlFor`/`id`. Required (not optional) — same a11y rule as Input: no unlabeled selects.

props.name: hideLabel
props.description: When `true`, visually hides the label while keeping it in the accessibility tree as the select's accessible name — use for compact contexts like a table cell.

props.name: error
props.description: Validation error message. When set, renders a `role="alert"` message below the select and marks the select `aria-invalid` with `aria-describedby` pointing at it.

props.name: options
props.description: The list of selectable options, rendered in order as native `<option>` elements.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Optional placeholder text shown as a disabled, hidden first option (value `''`) when no real option has been chosen yet.

components.example:
<Select
  label="Country"
  placeholder="Select a country"
  options={[
    { value: 'us', label: 'United States' },
    { value: 'ca', label: 'Canada' },
  ]}
  value={country}
  onChange={(e) => setCountry(e.target.value)}
/>

components.name: Spinner
components.description: An animated indicator that communicates an in-progress, indeterminate operation (e.g. data fetching or async form submission). Reach for it whenever content isn't ready to render yet and you need to signal that work is happening.
components.notes: The root element uses `role="status"` so assistive technology announces the `label` text as a live region update; the icon itself is purely visual.

props.name: size
props.description: Size of the spinning icon. One of `'sm' | 'base' | 'lg' | 'xl'`. Defaults to `'base'`.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label announced to screen readers via the `status` live region; not shown visually. Defaults to `'Loading'`.

components.name: Table
components.description: Renders tabular data with a horizontally-scrollable wrapper for narrow viewports. Compose it with TableHead, TableBody, TableRow, TableHeaderCell, and TableCell to build the table structure explicitly, the same way you would with plain HTML table elements.

components.name: TableBody
components.description: Semantic wrapper for a table's body row group (`<tbody>`). Use it to group the data TableRow/TableCell elements.

components.name: TableCell
components.description: A standard data cell (`<td>`) within a TableRow.

components.name: TableHead
components.description: Semantic wrapper for a table's header row group (`<thead>`). Use it to group the TableRow/TableHeaderCell elements that make up the column headings.

components.name: TableHeaderCell
components.description: A header cell (`<th>`) identifying a column (or row) within a TableRow.
components.notes: Defaults the native `scope` attribute to `'col'` if not provided; pass `scope="row"` for row headers.

components.name: TableRow
components.description: A single row (`<tr>`) within a TableHead or TableBody.

components.name: ToastProvider
components.description: Provides the `toast()` API (via ToastContext) to its subtree and renders the queued toasts into a portal at `document.body`. Wrap your application (or the relevant subtree) once near the root; descendants then call `useToast()` to queue notifications.
components.notes: The toast viewport is rendered with `aria-live="polite"`, so assistive technology announces new toasts without stealing focus. Each toast auto-dismisses after its `duration` (see ToastOptions) and can also be dismissed manually via the underlying `Alert`'s dismiss control.

props.name: children
props.description: The subtree that gains access to the `toast()` API via `useToast()`.

components.name: useToast
components.description: Reads the toast API from context, giving components a `toast()` function to queue toast notifications. Must be called from a descendant of `ToastProvider`.
components.notes: Throws: If called outside of a `ToastProvider`.

returns.description: A ToastContextValue containing the `toast` function used to queue notifications.

types.name: AlertVariant
types.description: Visual style of an Alert, which also determines its icon and ARIA role.

types.name: DateRangeValue
types.description: The current start/end selection of a DateRangePicker, as ISO date strings (`YYYY-MM-DD`, matching the native `<input type="date">` format).

fields.name: start
fields.description: Start of the range, as an ISO date string (`YYYY-MM-DD`).

fields.name: end
fields.description: End of the range, as an ISO date string (`YYYY-MM-DD`).

types.name: IconName
types.description: Names of the icons available to render via `<Icon name="..." />`.

types.name: IconSize
types.description: Available rendered sizes for Icon, mapped to CSS modifier classes.

types.name: SelectOption
types.description: A single choice rendered as a native `<option>` inside a Select.

fields.name: value
fields.description: Value submitted/reported for this option (the native `option` value).

fields.name: label
fields.description: Text displayed to the user for this option.

fields.name: disabled
fields.description: When `true`, renders the option disabled so it cannot be chosen.

types.name: ToastContextValue
types.description: The value returned by useToast — currently just the `toast()` function.

fields.name: toast
fields.description: Queues a new toast with the given options. Resolves immediately; the toast is dismissed automatically after `duration` ms (or manually if `duration` is 0).

types.name: ToastOptions
types.description: Options passed to `toast()` (from useToast) describing a single toast notification.

fields.name: title
fields.description: Optional heading rendered as the toast's title.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Main message content of the toast.

fields.name: variant
fields.description: Visual style of the toast, forwarded to the underlying `Alert`. Defaults to `Alert`'s default variant.

fields.name: duration
fields.description: Milliseconds before the toast auto-dismisses. Pass 0 to require a manual dismiss. Defaults to 5000.
